body: Mumbai-based investor, sometimes called a 'big whale' of Indian small caps (nickname not verified in sources found), a past business associate of Rakesh Jhunjhunwala (folklore-grade details). Public portfolio (holdings >1% disclosed quarterly): ~45-49 stocks worth roughly Rs 2,900-3,000 crore in 2025-26 data, with Shaily Engineering Plastics among top holdings; past widely cited winners include Atul Auto, Polycab, KPIT, Majesco and Safari Industries (returns not verified here). Edge (structural): sizable capital, willingness to take 1-3% stakes in tiny companies (including SME-platform and pre-IPO deals) and hold through illiquidity; network access to managements. Process (as described in media): many small bets on early-growth, often niche-manufacturing or tech-services small caps, letting winners run while losers stay small - a venture-style portfolio. Mistakes: several holdings have fallen 50%+ in smallcap drawdowns (2018-19, 2025) and some SME/micro positions lacked governance quality (characterisation, unverified). Copying risk: disclosures appear 2-6 weeks after quarter-end, only above 1%, and news of 'Kacholia buys' often causes 5-20% jumps - so followers buy after the price moves and never see his exits in time. Copyable: the portfolio construction idea (many small, equal-risk bets in early growth stories, add only on proof) rather than the tickers.

data.copyable: venture-style many-small-bets construction; not ticker cloning

title: Ashish Kacholia - diversified early-stage smallcap bets (India)
